newsitem.title: NORWAY: UBN may form joint insurer with Fokus, Codan - report.
newsitem.headline: UBN may form joint insurer with Fokus, Codan - report.

text.p: Savings bank Union Bank of Norway (UBN) may form a joint insurance company with commercial bank Fokus Bank and Danish insurer Codan Forsikring, Norwegian daily Aftenposten said on Monday.
It said the plan hinged on Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 Norwegian savings banks, failing in its attempt to take over Fokus.
"The moment Sparebankgruppen throws in the towel we will set in motion the cooperation plans," UBN spokesman Frode Helgerud told the newspaper.
Sparebankgruppen said last Friday it was extending by six weeks its 73 crowns per share bid to shareholders in Fokus.
On May 7, UBN and Fokus announced plans to establish cooperation in banking. They also said they would launch a joint cooperation in insurance with Codan.
The initiative for the cooperation came from Fokus, whose board is fighting the takeover attempt by Sparebankgruppen.
The three parties have been reluctant to elaborate on the insurance plans, but Helgerud said they would most probably set up a joint insurance company, according to Aftenposten.
The Norwegian Finance Ministry in March formally approved of a plan by Fokus and Codan to set up a joint life insurer.
Helgerud said UBN's own insurance business was small.
"By cooperating with Fokus and Codan we will quickly be able to achieve a new position," he told Aftenposten.
Fokus Bank is Norway's fourth biggest bank and UBN, known locally as Sparebanken NOR, is the third largest. UBN is also the biggest savings bank of Norway.
